articleTitle: Multi Parameter Integrated Measurement Method and Experimental Verification for Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The transmission lines are the important component of power grid, and the status monitoring is of great significance for ensuring the safe and stable operation of the power system. The current monitoring system is mostly for monitoring a single physical quantity, which has the shortcomings of low integration, high monitoring cost and difficult maintenance in the later stage, which is not suitable for the development of power internet of things. Therefore, this paper designs a multi physical intelligent sensing terminal to measure multiple parameters such as voltage, current, and galloping state of transmission lines. and builds a transmission line test platform to test the system performance. A transmission line testing platform was built to verify the system performance, mainly including the transient steady-state performance of voltage and current, as well as the galloping performance. The experiments showed that the multi parameter measurement system can work stably and reliably in a simulated transmission line environment, and has the characteristics of miniaturization, multi sensing, and integration.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of the Impact of Complex Time-Varying Harmonics on Commutation Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Following a large disturbance in the power system, the voltage often experiences a temporary drop, simultaneously triggering a large number of harmonic components. This phenomenon can lead to commutation failure and even direct current blocking, threating the system stability and safety. To accurately predict and rapidly prevent commutation failure, it is crucial to analyze the impact of the time-varying harmonics on the commutation process. Based on wideband measurement data and commutation area (CA) theory, this paper quantitatively analyzes the impact of harmonics on the commutation area under normal operation condition and fault condition. The results indicate that the calculation of commutation area considering time-varying harmonic effects can more accurately reflect the commutation area.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Electricity Market and Incentive-based Demand Response Management: A Stackelberg Game-based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper presents a study on a resource trading process aimed at assisting the grid operator (GO) in managing system imbalances during the intra-day market. The research incorporates two types of incentives, taking into account the perspectives of service providers (SPs) and the GO. The in-teractions among the entities involved are modelled using the Stackelberg game, while Stackelberg equilibrium (SE) is achieved through a distributed algorithm utilizing local information only. The numerical analysis indicates that demand response (DR) programs play a crucial role in enabling the GO to operate the power system reliably and economically. Moreover, a comparison between the two case studies reveals that implementing shorter timeframes for DR programs can yield enhanced demand reduction by residential consumers (RCs), resulting in potential cost savings and increased revenue for service providers facilitated by effective incentives. These results highlight the value of DR programs as a valuable tool for the GO in optimizing power system operations.

articleTitle: DAB LCC Resonant Converter Triple Phase Shift Control Bi-directional Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper presents the triple phase shift control method of the dual active bridge (DAB) LCC resonant converter for bi-directional high-efficiency wireless power transfer (WPT) applications in full operation range. The battery current amplitude feedback control regulates the primary side H-bridge internal phase shift angle. The battery side equivalent AC impedance is controlled at optimal value by regulating the battery side H-bridge internal phase shift angle. The phase shift angle amplitude between the two H-bridges is set to 90°. The power flow direction change is realized by simultaneously swapping the two internal phase shift angles together with the PWM modulator output gating signals to ensure the power is transferred from the phase leading H-bridge to the phase lagging H-bridge. The proposed DAB LCC resonant converter bi-directional battery charging and discharging control method has been verified in the PLECS circuit simulation and DC/DC converter hardware test.

articleTitle: Deep-Learning based Multiple Class Events Detection and Classification using Micro-PMU Data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Real-time analysis of multiple class events is necessary for enhanced situational awareness and safe operation of the power distribution networks. The deep-learning-based data-driven techniques for multiple-class event analysis have not been explored in the literature. Thus, we proposed a deep learning-based data-driven method to detect events from large real-time data. The convolutional auto-encoder helps in the exact time of event detection and temporal localization using time-series voltage and current magnitude phasors. Then, we proposed a deep-learning-based data-driven event classifier for effective multiple-class event classification. Three-phase voltage and current magnitude features are selected as input into the multi-class LSTM (long short-term memory) classifier model. Based on the research, a unique time series voltage and current magnitude pattern is generated from the different classes of events. With the help of the proposed algorithm, five classes of events can be effectively detected and classified using the measured voltage and current magnitude phasors. In this perspective, the proposed multi-class LSTM classifier is trained and tested with IEEE-34 node test feeder, which are simulated in a testbed setup including real-time digital simulator (RTDS), hardware µPMUs, hardware distribution phasor data concentrator (DPDC), and network switches. The outcomes verify that the proposed algorithm has high accuracy (100%) and requires only voltage and current magnitude phasors.

articleTitle: Analyzing & Benchmarking Rooftop Solar PV Deployment: Creating an Index for Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The importance of Rooftop solar segment lies in its potential to transform the energy landscape, offering cleaner more sustainable and affordable energy solutions while contributing to the environment, economy, and society as a whole. This paper presents the qualitative development of a comprehensive Rooftop Solar PV Index framework that employs a design thinking approach to analyze and benchmark the rooftop solar PV sector through the tenets of user desirability, technical feasibility & business viability. The index aims to address the multifaceted challenges hindering widespread adoption of Rooftop Solar PV by incorporating design thinking principles into the creation process.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Graph Hybrid Neural Network for PV Power Forecast
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Amid the bloom of Renewable energy sources (RES) integration into the electrical grid, an accurate power generation forecast is essential for a proper energy management plan to ensure power system reliability. Nevertheless, most previous studies have concentrated on predictors designed for centralized PV farms, often falling short of effectively accommodating distributed PV systems. Hence, this paper proposes a Graph- based architecture, namely Graph Convolutional Long Shortterm Memory Neural Network (GCLNN) for multi-site PV power forecast. Using the Graph Attention Mechanism, the adjacency matrix is constructed, representing the correlation between variables. From that, the weight of each parameter of the input data is determined, takes part in the training process, and improves the forecasting accuracy. For a practical indication of the proposed model's superiority, a multi-site dataset consists of the historical output power of three different neighboring PV systems in Ha Tinh, Vietnam. From the experimental result, the proposed model brings out outstanding accuracy, especially in higher time-step forecasts compared to the benchmark models.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Wind Turbine with Dynamic Fault Tree Based on Markov Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The traditional fault tree analysis method uses static gates such as “and gate”, “not gate”, “or gate” to model the fault tree and analyze the reliability of wind turbines. However, due to the current iteration of wind turbines, the traditional fault tree analysis method can not accurately describe the relationship between the failures of the components of the wind turbines, and it is easy to cause the reliability evaluation results of wind turbines to be unreliable. Therefore, in this paper, Markov chain and dynamic fault tree analysis method are used to analyze the reliability analysis process of wind turbines. Firstly, the dynamic fault tree logic gate is used to construct the system fault tree, and then the fault relationship of different components of wind turbine is connected by Markov chain and its state transition characteristics. Finally, after the dynamic fault tree is transformed into Markov chain with continuous parameters, the probability calculation formula can be derived according to the state transition graph to evaluate the reliability. The numerical results show that this method can improve the accuracy of dynamic reliability evaluation of wind turbines.

articleTitle: Online Data Acquisition and Storage for Rooftop Solar System Utilizing Time Series Databases and Cloud-based Visualization Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Renewable energy sources, especially solar PV, are emerging as one of the most promising solutions to combat the global warming phenomenon and climate change. However, solar PV systems often require proper supervision due to their depen-dence on various environmental factors. In practice, supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems have been widely adopted to capture PV system parameters and store them for long-term accessibility. This study proposes a comprehensive so-lution for monitoring rooftop PV systems, including data logging, storage, and backup. The authors also provide a cloud-based service to access the database and visualize measurements in real-time as our main contributions. The conclusions suggest future improvements and recommend several practical applications utilizing our resources.

articleTitle: Data Driven Fault Monitoring of Wind Farm Gearbox
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: As one of the key components of wind turbines, the gearbox usually has a high failure rate and long downtime due to long-term operation and operating conditions. This study aims to comprehensively consider various data such as temperature, wear, and stress, and adopt a fault monitoring technology based on neural network methods to improve the accuracy and reliability prediction of the operation status of wind power gearboxes. With the continuous accumulation of actual data, we can continuously optimize the parameters of neural network models, thereby achieving data-driven model optimization. This means that we can update and modify the model based on the new data collected during actual operation, so that it can better adapt to different working conditions and environmental changes. Ultimately, through this research method, we can more effectively manage the gearbox of wind farms, reduce downtime, optimize maintenance plans, and thereby improve the reliability and operational efficiency of the entire wind power system.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power Generation Forecasting Based on Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Since the 14th Five-Year Plan, the strategy of “carbon neutrality and carbon peak” has become one of the important strategies to realize China's economic and environmental development, and the clean energy structure will be the main way to achieve the double carbon goal. Solar energy has become one of the important energy sources because of its large resource amount and wide distribution range, and photovoltaic power generation technology is an important means to control solar power generation. The accuracy of photovoltaic power generation prediction plays an important role in the allocation and use of energy, so as to maximize the use of energy. However, unlike the continuous adjustable and controllable traditional power generation, solar power generation cannot be accurately controlled, and it has a great randomness, which brings great challenges to photovoltaic power generation. In order to make full use of solar energy resources and ensure the real-time balance of power generation, transmission and consumption of the power system when photovoltaic power generation is connected to the grid, it is crucial to accurately predict the power of photovoltaic power generation. In order to solve the problems of unsatisfactory prediction accuracy and poor robustness when training set missing data, this paper adopts K-means algorithm for similar day screening and combines it with random forest algorithm(RF) to construct a photovoltaic power generation prediction model. Through similar day screening, more accurate and applicable prediction models can be obtained for forecasting days;at the same time, the robustness of the model is improved by using random forest model. Through verification with data from a power plant in Wuhan, Hubei Province, the accuracy and stability of K-means-RF algorithm in photovoltaic power generation prediction are proved.

articleTitle: Pulse Width Modulation (PWM)-Controlled Wireless Power Transfer using Mu-Negative Metamaterials and Ferrite Shielding on a Four-Coil Layered Double-D (LDD) System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems rarely include shielding on their prototypes. The proposal combines ferrite tiles, 3D-printed metamaterials, and circuitry to develop a high- efficiency transfer. Objectives include: (1) to design layered ‘double-D’ (DD) coils and metamaterial slabs for the system with ferrite tiles for shielding; (2) to model a PWM-controlled inductance double capacitance series and parallel capacitance (LCC-SP); (3) to build a working prototype based on the model with the ferrite tile, designed metamaterial slab and layered DD coil; and (4) to determine the efficiency, transfer distance, and coupling coefficient of the prototype. The researchers used a portable oscilloscope to measure the relevant parameters concerning power transfer. An increase in efficiency and coupling coefficient was attained with the proposed WPT system.

articleTitle: EV Scheduling Optimization by Utilizing Excess Photovoltaic Energy with Forward Dynamic Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: As the global trend toward sustainable transportation gains momentum, electric vehicles (EVs) have become increasingly popular due to their ecological advantages. However, as the EV population expands, issues pertaining to power quality, such as voltage stability and load profiles, have emerged. Various solutions have been proposed to mitigate the adverse effects of EV charging. One such approach involves the amalgamation of renewable energy sources (RES) within charging infrastructure, coupled with Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology. In this article, a new method is presented that utilizes RES in conjunction with the Forward Dynamic Programming Algorithm to lower the cost of charging all EVs. This approach also works to even out the demand curve by considering EV owners' travel schedules.

articleTitle: Comparison of Different V2G Configurations for A Microgrid System in Terms of Different Ancillary Service Controls
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: A microgrid system able to supply 15 households was established in Xiaolin Village in Taiwan. Each house consists of 3kW solar photovoltaic panels and 6–10 kWh battery modules. Moreover, a 100 kWh energy storage container (see Fig. 1) is installed for power balance. As the number of electric vehicles (EVs) in Taiwan gradually increases, the batteries of these EVs become important resources for grid operations. Therefore, it is crucial to explore technologies like Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Battery-to-Grid (B2G) and how they can be implemented in the Xiaolin microgrid. The chargin station needs to be carefully designed so that it can well coordinate with existing energy storage and PV systems. The objective of this paper is twofold. Firstly, some of the ancillary service control functions will be implemented in inverters to achieve either V2G or B2G. Secondly, we will investigate two types of configurations that V2G or B2G can be implemented in the Xiaolin microgrid and see which one has the best contribution to the grid. From the results presented in the paper, we can conclude that a centralized inverter, capable of providing V2G services, EV charging, power conversion, and balancing can offer a cheaper and coherent control performance. Nevertheless, efforts needs to be devoted to keep the centralized inverter to maintain operational for system reliability.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of the MF /PCM Based Ocean Thermal Engine Using OpenFOAM
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Capturing ocean thermal energy through the volume change of the phase change materials (PCMs) is a promising method for in-situ energy supply in the deep-sea environment. Due to the low thermal conductivity of PCM, the metal foam (MF) is widely used to enhance heat transfer inside PCMs. This study focuses on an MF/PCM based ocean thermal engine for achieving thermoelectric conversion. A numerical model of the solid-liquid phase change and pressure change process inside ocean thermal engines is proposed. The advantage of this model is that it takes into account the impact of system pressure on the PCM physical properties, and the nature convection process is solved directly without using any empirical equations to ensure the accuracy. An in-house code for solving the proposed model was developed using OpenFOAM and the experimental work was conducted for model validation. Results show that the developed code has good accuracy and convergency. Based on the numerical simulation, the influence of pressure parameters on the energy conversion process and output power of the engine was discussed.

articleTitle: Enhancing Vertical Axis Wind Turbine Performance Investigation at Low Wind Speed Using Electrical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This research provides an objective for a new approach to increase the hybrid Savonius-Darrieus Tip Speed Ratio range in a low-wind speed experiment (0–12 m/s) by considering the effect of power loss from the DC generator used. The models used are hybrid Savonius-Darrieus and single Darrieus with 4 blades. 2 stages of Savonius with 0.2 overlap and a 135° bucket angle are used as internal rotors, while the external rotor is a NREL S809 Darrieus airfoil with a cord length of 7 cm. A DC generator with a maximum voltage of 12 V is used. The friction, copper, and iron loss coefficients of the DC generator are 4.131, and 0.013, respectively. In the low wind speed experiment, the maximum Tip Speed Ratio that can be measured is around 1. Furthermore, by applying the improvement method in measurement, which involves applying constant current and variable voltage, the Tip Speed Ratio can reach 3.5-4. Thus, according to the findings, the hybrid Savonius-Darrieus and single Darrieus have maximum Power Coefficients of 0.30 at the Tip Speed Ratio of 1.5 and 0.33 at the Tip Speed Ratio of 3.3, respectively.

articleTitle: Influence of Power Electronic Devices Failure Rate on Wind Turbine System Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the influence of failure rate variation of power electronic devices on the reliability of wind turbine system. Based on the relationship between device failure rate and system reliability, the relationship between them is studied. This paper presents an idea of linking power electronics and wind power system reliability calculation. Additionally, the calculation methods of failure rates for systems with different connection modes, including series system and parallel system, are also described. Finally, a numerical case study using non-sequential Monte Carlo method is carried out to verify the degree of influence of device failure rate on system reliability. The analysis shows that the different degree of equipment failure rate will have a non-negligible impact on the fan system. Therefore, changes in the failure rate of power electronics need to be considered in the reliability assessment of the fan system.

articleTitle: Short-Term PV Power Forecasting Based on LSTM and Multi-Head Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel hybrid model for accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting, integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network and multi-head attention mechanism. The model is trained and evaluated using a dataset from the Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC), covering diverse weather conditions. A comprehensive data preprocessing workflow, including correlation analysis, normalization, outlier detection, missing value imputation, and sliding window mechanism, ensures robustness and generalization. Bayesian optimization is employed for hyperparameter tuning. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance compared to common models across various weather conditions.

articleTitle: Transient Flow Dynamics Analysis of a Large Prototype Francis Turbine at Different Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: It is important to study the dynamic characteristics of flow transients in prototype Francis turbines as they play a vital role in understanding and optimizing turbine performance, ensuring stability and reliability, and preventing flow-induced structural vibration problems in hydropower plants. In this study, a prototype of a large-scale low-head Francis turbine installed in a hydropower plant is used to study its flow transient dynamics. The site measurement was conducted and the pressure levels in the inlet and outlet of the unit at various operating conditions were obtained. Using the measured data to set up the boundary conditions of the unsteady CFD calculations, and analyze the flow dynamics in the turbine channels at different operating conditions. The results show that pressure from the spiral case inlet to the draft tube outlet is a gradual downward trend at all loads. At 25% load, the guide vane opening is relatively small, a high-speed water ring is formed in the vaneless space, and a turbulent flow appears in the draft tube. With the increase of the guide vane opening, the high-speed water ring in the vaneless space gradually disappears. At 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> load, the flow line is very smooth in the whole flow passage and the flow rate reaches the maximum value at the runner inlet. The calculated pressure distributions of the turbine flow domain under different operating conditions can be applied to the finite element model of the runner to study its flow-induced structural dynamics characteristics. The obtained results and conclusions provide references for the optimal operation of low-head Francis turbine units in other different power plants.

articleTitle: Supervised Machine Learning and Current Signal Based Universal Fault Protection Strategy for Distributed Generation Integrated into Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Distributed Generations (DGs) play a significant role in the modern electric power grid, offering benefits such as reduced transmission and distribution losses and minimized environmental impact. Globally, solar Photovoltaic (PV) and Wind Turbine Distributed Generators (WTDGs) have become some of the most widely utilized DG resources, driven by their improving efficiency, and advancing technology. However, from the viewpoint of power system protection, the integration of these resources into power systems poses various significant challenges for protective relays. These relays traditionally rely on both voltage and current measurements and and may not operate correctly in the presence of WTDGs. To address these issues, the use of a current-only protection system with a unified supervised Machine Learning (ML) classifier for directional and phase selection relays is proposed in this work. The comparative analysis shows the superiority of the Random Forest classifier in using only currents and being able to detect both the fault direction with perfect accuracy and the faulty phase(s) with over 92% accuracy, making it suitable for implementation in both transmission and distribution networks, including WTDGs resources.

articleTitle: Power Sharing Enhancement of Standalone Microgrid using Primary Control Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimized droop control employing the Centripetal Force-Gravity Search Algorithm (CF-GSA), a metaheuristic multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. The proposed method aims to enhance droop performance, focusing on power sharing, voltage and frequency stability, and power quality. CF-GSA, specifically designed to address local solution issues common in optimization algorithms, has been demonstrated to be effective and superior through a series of simulations. The simulation results affirm the proposed multi-objective optimization droop control method's capability to rectify issues arising from power sharing errors in isolated AC MGs dealing with high inductive loads and changes in line impedance.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Optimal Generation Scheduling Applying Uncertainty in Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Microgrids provide efficient means of incorporating renewable energy resources (RES) into the power network. The deployment of an energy management system into a microgrid is essential for achieving efficient utilization of resources and ensuring stable grid operation at a favorable cost. However, the inherent intermittent nature of consumer loads and RES introduces uncertainty, posing significant challenges for system design. This paper proposes a generation scheduling approach that can optimally manage energy resources in a microgrid in the presence of load and generation uncertainties. First, a data-driven machine learning algorithm is employed to forecast PV and wind generation as well as electrical power demand from weather data and actual dataset. Next, optimal unit commitment based on energy prices to minimize system costs is conducted using Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP). This approach provides optimal generation scheduling among PV and wind turbine generation systems as well as the required power from the utility grid. Simulation results for different case studies is carried out in order to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method for hourly RES and load profile forecast. Furthermore, results indicate that optimal generation scheduling can be effective in minimizing the operating cost under the worst-case of RES and load uncertainty.

articleTitle: Generation System Reliability Evaluation Considering Time-Varying Wind Speeds Based on Markov Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Traditional power generation methods, such as thermal power and nuclear power, can provide stable and reliable power to the load. With the increasing maturity of new energy generation technologies, more and more renewable energy sources, such as wind and solar power generation, have been incorporated into the power grid. However, compared with traditional energy sources, one of the characteristics of renewable energy is uncertainty. For wind turbine generator (WTG), the change of wind speed is the main factor leading to the change of their output power. Uncertain wind power output will reduce the reliability of the power system into which wind power is integrated and increase the system operation cost, so it is necessary to study the reliability of wind power. In this paper, the reliability of a power system containing different percentages of wind turbines is evaluated by establishing a forced outage rate (FOR) for wind turbines, taking into account wind turbine mechanical failure factors and wind speed. The study proposes a simple reliability assessment method that can be used in the planning stage of power systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of 13-Level Cascaded H-Bridge Multilevel Inverter Using Sinusoidal Switching Angle Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: A highly effective solution for medium voltage and high power applications is the multilevel inverter. Since it is not possible to directly link the power semiconductor switch to the high voltage network, the demand for Multilevel Inverters is rising. The fact that the THD (Total Harmonic Distortion) of these output-voltage waveforms decreases as the number of levels grows is one of the most crucial characteristics of the multilevel Inverter. This paper presents an experimental study on a 13-level cascade H-bridge multilevel inverter incorporating sinusoidal angle modulation technique. The study highlights the advantages of multilevel inverters and provides insights into voltage waveform quality, harmonic distortion, and overall system performance. Also the simulation analysis has been performed using PSIM software. The Inverter system has been developed by IGBT and Arduino Mega 2560 controller for creating PWM pulses. Experimental results have been compared with simulation results. The experimental validation confirms the accuracy and feasibility of the proposed modulation techniques. This research contributes to the advancement of multilevel inverter technology and offers guidance for future applications.

articleTitle: An Analysis and Optimisation of the Addition of BESS to Produce Hydrogen from Seawater
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This article presents the development and implementation of an optimisation model to size the components of a system to produce green hydrogen from desalinated sea water, in order to determine the effect that BESS (and particularly its cost) would have on the sizing of other components. A linear optimisation model was successfully produced in Pyomo in the Python environment, and used a PEM electrolyser, lithium BESS, Solar PV and a reverse osmosis desalination plant as inputs. The results show that if a daily amount of hydrogen needs to be produced, BESS enhances the plant operational characteristics with BESS capital costs not drastically impacting the overall capital cost. This is because the BESS allows a smaller electrolyser to be utilised and be ran for extended periods of time than just PV generation would allow. It also allows production to still occur on the few days with low solar production even within a desert environment. Furthermore, cost and energy-wise, the desalination component of the system is a small percentage.

articleTitle: Study on the Orientation of the Cascade Latent Heat Storage for Real-time Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Due to high energy density, latent heat storage technologies are capturing the attention of researchers worldwide. The downsides of storage media's significantly low thermal conductivity can be overcome by various methods, and cascade storage is one of them. In the existing literature, charging and discharging of multi-PCM (cascade latent heat storage) are analyzed separately. In this study, efforts are made to understand the actual behavior of multi-PCM systems for simultaneous charging and discharging. This research investigates the potential of cascade latent heat storage for medium-temperature solar thermal applications such as solar cooking. The comparative investigation between single (NaNO3) and multiple PCM-based (NaNO3 and NaNO2) storages is done for simultaneous melting and solidification cycles. A melting rate augmentation of 2.6 times is observed in cascade storage compared to the NaNO3 storage in real-time operation. Furthermore, it is observed that horizontal cascade storage outshines the vertical cascade storage by 20.2% in terms of melting rate.

articleTitle: Decentralized Sustainable Energy Production through Biomass Gasification-CHP System Using Coconut Waste
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Abundant use of palm waste in the renewable energy landscape, resulting in seasonal variation issues. To overcome these challenges and ensure sustainability in the future renewable energy scenario, coconut shell (CS) was introduced as an alternative agricultural waste, and its performance was compared with regular palm waste (palm kernel shell, PKS) in terms of net electricity generation and electrical efficiency. A simulations flowsheet was constructed based on downdraft gasification combined-heat and power system (Ga-CHP) with a focus on two key parameters for sensitivity analysis: temperature and equivalence ratio (ER). The results revealed that the maximum net electrical generation for CS and PKS was observed at 850°C and 1000°C, respectively. At these temperatures, the net electricity generation of the CS and PKS were reported to be at 20.16 kWh and 18.99 kWh. On the other hand, maximum net electricity generation and electrical efficiency were achieved by both PKS and CS at an equivalence ratio of 0.5, where the maximum net electricity generation for CS is 27.32 kWh and PKS is 34.58 kWh, and the electrical efficiency of CS is 28.97% and 36.11% for PKS. Through this study, it is suggested that the incorporation of CS as an alternative to palm waste can contribute to a more stable and sustainable electricity generation in the renewable energy sector.

articleTitle: Algorithm Design for the Different Programs of HVDC Control and Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: As the core of HVDC(High Voltage Direct Current) project., the control and protection program is the key to the engineering upgrade and transformation process. The lack of a visual analysis and description method for differences before and after page modification in program. Modification can only be verified through program modification form filled out by engineering personnel., which can easily lead to inconsistencies such as omissions and errors. This article is based on the HCM3000 DC control and protection platform., and designs a analysis algorithm for different programs of the control and protection. By parsing the application files of the control and protection program., a class multiple linked list is generated., and data processing is performed to generate a binary decomposition tree structure. Then., node matching is performed on the data structure chain based on the binary decomposition tree to ultimately achieve differential information comparison and ensure the accuracy of the control and protection program on the engineering site. The developed software has been applied in HVDC projects., greatly improving the reliability of project operation.

articleTitle: Comparative Study with Analysis of Fixed-Tilt and Tracked Solar Photovoltaic Panels
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper discusses the performance analysis of three different systems: fixed tilt, single-axis, and dual axis solar tracking system. MATLAB Simulink is used to model power generation and cost equations. The paper proposes a single design to perform three different configurations, namely, single, dual and fixed axils. Two testing scenarios have been used: sunny and partly cloudy days to validate and increase the accuracy level of the obtained results. Simulink, also, has been used to compare the theoretical and empirical results. Both theoretical and experimental results show that the dual axis has more generated power, but it is less difference with single axis. The results show the single axis tracking system has good economic value compared to dual axis.

articleTitle: Social Sustainability Assessment of Energy Systems: Research Status and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In pursuit of sustainable development, the energy sector must consider the three basic pillars of sustainability: economic, environmental, and social. However, research on the social sustainability pillar has been lagging relative to the two other pillars. This paper explores the status and opportunities in the field of social sustainability assessment of energy systems through a systematic literature review of 122 peer-reviewed articles. The paper primarily highlights the common research gaps identified in existing literature, the definition of social sustainability as defined by previous research, and the tools used to measure social sustainability. The findings of this paper can guide researchers and other stakeholders about future research directions and serve as a knowledge base in the field of social sustainability assessment of energy systems.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Coil Distance Variation on the Performance of Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper delves into a comprehensive examination of the Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system, specifically exploring the impact of varying coil distances on its performance. The positioning of coils within the WPT framework plays a pivotal role in influencing key parameters such as efficiency, resonant frequency, and bandwidth. Our study seeks to contribute to the existing body of knowledge on WPT by designing and implementing an experimental test rig for a WPT circuit configuration. Building upon extensive preliminary research, we conducted experiments rooted in the fundamentals of resonant WPT, incorporating essential components such as an inverter, coils, and rectifier. The findings reveal a discernible correlation between coil distance and WPT performance, with an observed decrease in efficiency as the distance between coils increases. This observation underscores the substantial impact that variations in coil distance can exert on the overall efficacy of WPT systems. Through meticulous experimentation and analysis, our study sheds light on crucial insights that can inform the optimization and design of WPT technologies, ultimately advancing the field's understanding and application.

articleTitle: Fault Warning and Reliability Analysis of Wind Turbine Failure Based on Data-driven
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The global wind power industry is growing rapidly and wind energy has become an integral part of the power system. In order to improve the stability of wind turbine generators (WTGs), it is essential to accurately predict and warn of their operational status. Today, most WTGs are equipped with monitoring and data acquisition systems that can collect and record comprehensive operational status information, providing a reliable source of data for assessing the unit's operational status. Effectively analysing the data and providing early warnings of faults is a key issue in the study of the stable operation of wind farms. In this study, historical and real-time wind turbine data, wind farm operation and maintenance data and meteorological data are used as samples. Firstly, a Weibull linear model is constructed to analyse the performance of the wind turbine and to map the power bands for reliable operation of the wind turbine. A wind turbine wind power prediction model was developed using a BP neural network prediction model, and then the predicted wind speed was used to obtain the power of the wind turbine, and the predicted power was compared with the normal power operating band. If the predicted power is within the power range, the wind turbine is highly reliable. If the predicted power is beyond the power range, the reliability is low, at this time, a warning signal should be issued and the monitoring of the turbine operation status should be strengthened.

articleTitle: DLMS/COSEM based Simulation Platform for Smart Meter Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This research paper introduces an IEC 62056 protocol based platform designed for real-time cyber-physical simulations of smart meter data within the smart grid domain. The platform serves as a comprehensive tool for researchers, enabling the simulation of various cyber attacks on smart meter data communication. Beyond cyber attack scenarios, the platform also facilitates the monitoring and visualization of real-time trends of diverse parameters communicated by smart meters. Its non-limiting capabilities extend to providing a database creation tool for specific loading conditions, offering researchers a platform for evaluating smart meter data security and performance under various loading scenarios.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Assessment of Development of Wind Farms at a Potential Location in Eastern Region of Saudi Arabia - A Step towards Alternative Energy for Sustainable Future
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The present study has investigated the techno-economic feasibility to develop 15 MW wind-energy-farm at Qaisumah, Eastern-Province, Saudi-Arabia (SA) based on analysis of long-term wind-speed data. Qaisumah is a potential wind-energy resource. The analyzed data shows that monthly-average-wind-speed (MAWS) of Qaisumah (28<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">º</sup>20‘ N, 46º07’ E) lies in between 3.5 and 4.6m/s at height of 10m. The simulations of wind-farms encompass combinations of 600kW commercial wind-machinery (CWMs, 50m hub-height). Feasibility assessment was performed by employing HOMER-Energy's (NREL's) HOMER-software. The study results presented include monthly wind-speed changes, FD-profiles (frequency-distribution-profiles) of wind-speed, month-wise and annual quantity of generated-energy from the 15MW wind-farm (50m hub), cost of generation-of-energy (COE, US$-per-kWh), capacity-factor (percent), etc. The FD-profiles point out that wind-speeds are below 3m/s for about 43 percent of time during a year. This means commercial wind-electric-conversion-systems (WECS) would produce energy for approximately 57% of time during a year. About 23590 MWh of energy is produced from 15MW-WECS (with 50m hub-level) on annual-basis. The COE by utilizing 600kW (50m hub-level) is approximately 0.0487 US$-per-kWh. With installation of 15MW WECS, approximately 2026 tons of carbon emissions can be reduced annually. Various other factors (e.g. height-of-hub, capacity factor, etc.) for WECS-installation have also been taken into consideration.

articleTitle: Frequency Stability Assessment Method Based on Wide-Area Spatial-Temporal Information Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Receiving-end power grids with heavy loads necessitate the delivery of large amounts of power via high-voltage or ultra-high-voltage AC/DC lines to meet local energy demands. In this circumstance, once DC blocking or line failure occurs, the receiving-end power grid would be easily affected by frequency dips. Moreover, the process of frequency drop is extremely evolved rapidly, often leading to irreversible frequency instability within several to tens of seconds. Therefore, it is crucial to rapidly and accurately predict the frequency instability trend of the receiving-end power grid. Considering this issue, this paper proposes a frequency stability assessment method based on wide-area spatial-temporal information learning. The method integrates a spatial interpolation algorithm and deep neural networks to build a transient frequency stability assessment model. The model assesses the system frequency stability status accurately, achieves high computational efficiency, and can meet the requirements for online use. A case study using data from an actual grid is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Lattice Boltzmann modeling of water and supercritical CO2 flow in geothermal reservoir considering salt mass transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Supercritical CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and brine through geothermal reservoir pores is considered a multiphase flow of partially miscible CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and water, incorporating salt transport in the liquid phase fraction. A lattice Boltzmann model of pseudopotential flow with multiple components is adopted to study the multiphase flow. A continuous species transfer model at the phase interface characterizes the salt transport. The two models are coupled to investigate the pore permeation of multiphase flow between supercritical CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and brine. The findings of the simulations demonstrate that, in contrast to CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, the trend for water flow rate and relative permeability increases with increasing water saturation. Elevating the driving force causes both fluids' flow rates to rise noticeably. Flow rate and relative permeability of water expand with a solid's more hydrophobic surface while CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flux and relative permeability shrink. Water and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flow rates are both decreased by increased salinity because it is more difficult for water's flow and deformation.

articleTitle: Thermoeconomic Modeling, Analysis, and Comparison of Single Flash Cycle and Organic Rankine Cycle for Geothermal Power Generation in Montelago, Philippines
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The Philippines has abundant geothermal resources because of its advantageous location in the Pacific Ring of Fire. To address the country's increasing electricity demand, the Department of Energy is considering developing low-temperature resources for power generation. One of these resources is the geothermal field in Montelago, Mindoro, which has an average geothermal fluid temperature of 180°C - 200°C. Thermoeconomic analysis was applied to a single flash cycle and two configurations of organic Rankine cycle with various working fluids to evaluate the resource. The simulation of the cycle was done using the Engineering Equation Solver. Having the same operating conditions, the single flash cycle generates the highest power output of 5393 kW with a thermal and 2nd law efficiency of 4.86% and 23.77<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, respectively. The simple organic Rankine and organic Rankine cycles with an internal heat exchanger can produce a power of 4916 kW and 5106 kW, respectively. However, there are negative exergy rates in the organic Rankine cycle because of the low operating conditions for the two pressure sides of the cycle. A parametric study was conducted to determine the effect of the variation of the high-pressure side of the cycle on the plant's performance. Based on the result, the cycle that can produce the maximum power output is the organic Rankine cycle with an internal heat exchanger using isopentane, which can reach up to 9980 kW with a thermal and 2nd law efficiency of 14.56% and 53.27%, respectively.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Transient Frequency Stability Modeling and Analysis Based on ResNet and SHAP
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In recent years, China has been actively constructing new-type power systems to optimize the nation-wide energy structure and improve energy efficiency. As a result, ultra-high voltage(UHV) transmission has become increasingly popular, and the proportion of renewable energy in power systems has gradually increased. These phenomena have resulted in unprecedentedly complicated power grids with hybrid AC/DC interconnection structures, increased system uncertainty, and difficulty in maintaining a balance between power generation and load. In this context, system transient frequency stability is greatly challenged. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a method to model and analyze frequency stability characteristics of receiving-end power grids based on interpretable deep learning. First, the PSASP simulation software is employed to set up a series of representative operating conditions and transient faults to obtain sample data. Next, based on the simulated sample data, a residual convolutional neural network (ResNet) is utilized to predict the stability of frequency after a fault occurs in the power grid under the influence of AC-DC hybrid structure. Finally, the network prediction results are analyzed using the shapley additive explanations method (SHAP). The proposed method is verified with a realistic receiving-end system, which verifies its effectiveness and provides important guidance for follow-up frequency stability control measures.

articleTitle: A Study on the Construction of Charging Stations on Freeways Using a Road Section Power Consumption Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In recent years, China's new energy vehicles have developed rapidly, and more people choose new energy vehicles as a means of transportation. In order to meet the long-distance driving needs of new energy vehicles and take into account the need for early construction, State Grid Corporation has built charging stations in each service area of the highway (research section) in 2019. However, some service areas have idle charging stations, resulting in resource waste and long-term losses. Due to lack of maintenance in the later stage, some charging stations have been damaged, resulting in poor user experience and limiting the long-distance cross-regional driving of pure electric vehicles, ultimately affecting the subsequent development of new energy vehicles. On the other hand, with the increase in the number of electric vehicles, some highway charging stations have insufficient charging equipment, making it difficult to meet the charging needs, resulting in long queues and high charging time costs. Therefore, this article proposes a reasonable construction plan by constructing corresponding models and theoretical analysis. Firstly, the overview of the Jiangsu section of G15 (Shenhai Expressway) and the distribution of service areas were analyzed. Based on this, necessary parameters such as section length and traffic flow were defined, and a section power consumption model was constructed. The model was provided with data through intuitive observation, statistical analysis, historical comparison, and other methods. Based on predictive analysis, select electric vehicle data for 2030 and combine it with the road section power consumption model to analyze the power consumption of each road section, and then calculate the charging demand. Next, the operation of each charging station will be analyzed using the queuing theory model. When the waiting time for charging in the queue does not exceed 0.2 hours as a condition, the number of charging devices that need to be constructed in each service area will be calculated. By comparing with current data, the number of new charging devices that need to be constructed will be obtained. Finally, a plan for the construction of charging devices in each service area of the research section in the next seven years (2030) will be provided.

articleTitle: Research on Integrated Energy Microgrid Operation Considering P2G and CCS
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In order to realize the goals of sustainable energy use and low-carbon economic development, this paper analyzes the operating characteristics of cogeneration units, carbon capture and electricity-to-gas conversion equipment, proposes a combined operation mode of cogeneration units taking into account carbon capture and electricity-to-gas conversion technologies, analyzes the characteristics of the electricity-heat output of the cogeneration units and the carbon emissions under the mode, and establishes an integrated energy microgrid economic operation model under the joint operation mode taking into account the carbon trading. An economic operation model is developed for the integrated energy microgrid considering carbon trading under this combined operation mode. The example verifies the economy and carbon emission advantages of the integrated energy microgrid based on carbon capture and electricity-to-gas conversion technologies under four scenarios, which effectively reduces the carbon emission of the microgrid while minimizing the system operation cost. Compared with the traditional microgrid, the operating cost is reduced by 7776.84 yuan and the carbon emission is reduced by 2697.88 kg.

articleTitle: CityEnergyFlow Navigator: Optimizing Building-EV Coordinate Operation on Rooftop PV Self-Consumption Performance at City Scale
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Demand-side energy management centered around buildings is complex, involving rooftop photovoltaics(RPV) for power generation, energy storage devices such as batteries and ice storage systems, and the inherent flexibility of buildings themselves. In addition to traditional storage technologies, electric vehicles (EVs) are gaining attention as a new form of energy storage. However, EVs inherently exhibit uncertainties in spatiotemporal mobility and temporal variability in charging, adding greater complexity to energy management on the demand side. To address these challenges, this study proposes a city-level demand-side energy management system called CityEnergyFlow Navigator comprising the energy simulator Voyager, the visualization platform Panorama, and the experimental platform Pilot. The research focuses on the city of Shenzhen as a case study, encompassing 570,000 buildings and 470,000 EVs. Through simulations, it was found that buildings consumed 43,864,636,163 kWh, EVs consumed 712,582,586 kWh, RPV supplied 25,324,816,714 kWh, and the grid contributed 27,823,174,802 kWh of energy annually. Furthermore, the study proposes an optimization model to enhance the SCR of RPV systems through regulating the flexible resources. During the experimental period from the 116 to the 123 day, Base strategy with 470,000 EVs supporting unidirectional charging resulted in a RPV-SCR of 63.2%. However, when bidirectional charging was enabled for all EVs, the RPV-SCR increased to 76.6%. Considering the building area to ice storage energy capacity ratio of 7:1, Shenzhen city was projected to have 148,000,000 kWh ice storage units distributed among the buildings. With 470,000 EVs using default charging strategy, the RPV-SCR reached 92.3% using only these ice storage devices. Similarly, the RPV-SCR increased to 84.3% using only 28,000,000 kWh batteries. Remarkably, integrating all available flexible resources achieved an impressive RPV-SCR of 94.6%.

articleTitle: A Data-driven Probabilistic Calculation Method for Optimal Electricity-Hydrogen-Traffic Flows
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Aiming at an efficient distributed hydrogen supply network (DHSNs), this paper proposes a data-driven probabilistic calculation method for optimal electricity-hydrogen-traffic flows. Firstly, an optimal electricity-hydrogen-traffic flow model is established considering the couplings of mixed traffic flows on hydrogen and charging demand, power couplings, as well as inter-station hydrogen couplings by hydrogen tube trailers. Then, a data-driven probabilistic solving method based on polynomial chaos expansion is proposed, to improve the solving efficiency. The proposed method is established on the raw data of uncertainties, requiring no probability density function (PDF) information and effectively reducing the computation burdens and assuring accuracy stability by analytical computation based on the sparse grid-based Gaussian integration. Finally, case studies are carried out and verify a 43.25% improvement in overall profit and high accuracy of the probabilistic solving method.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Routing Algorithm Based on Energy Consumption for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Dynamic route planning for electric vehicle (EV) that takes energy consumption into account is essential for improving travel efficiency. The key is to consistently choose the most efficient route in a time-varying road network. This paper introduces a dynamic routing algorithm based on energy consumption (DR-EC) for electric vehicles, comprising three main steps. Firstly, we design a method for calculating dynamic weights of the road network based on the energy consumption model. Next, we propose an enhanced A* algorithm by incorporating directional angles. Finally, we demonstrate the DR-EC algorithm by combining it with the route update mechanism. We evaluate our method by comparing it with classical static route planning and dynamic route planning algorithms. The results indicate that the DR-EC algorithm can save up to 4.77% of time and 6.2% of energy compared to static planning. Furthermore, the DR-EC algorithm outperforms the compared dynamic planning algorithm in terms of travel time and travel energy at different departure times. This study provides theoretical support for the development of electric vehicles and the autonomous decision-making of intelligent vehicles.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Cooling and Heating Energy Consumption for PCM Integrated a Residential Building Envelope
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Latent heat thermal energy storage technologies using Phase Change Materials (PCMs) are a promising solution to enhance building thermal performance and reduce energy consumption. However, conducting experimental or numerical studies becomes time-consuming and computationally expensive due to the non-linearity and complexity associated with climatic conditions and variations in the thermophysical properties of PCMs within the building envelope. Thus, effective energy demand forecasting is essential for optimizing planning and minimizing energy consumption in buildings. Machine learning techniques have become increasingly popular due to their reliability and cost-effectiveness. This study uses machine learning models to predict the energy consumption of PCM-integrated residential building envelopes. Five well-known machine learning models were investigated: Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Generalized Additive Model (GAM), and Decision Tree (DT). These models considered PCM thermophysical properties, location, and thickness variations. The dataset was generated through a parametric analysis using EnergyPlus and JEplus simulation tools. The prediction computations were conducted using a computer program written in Python-based software. Thereafter, model performance was assessed using three metrics: R2, MAE, and RMSE. The results indicate that the ANN model outperformed others, achieving the lowest RMSE, MAE, and the highest R-squared value exceeding 0.99. Moreover, this study's findings emphasize the potential of the ANN model in predicting energy consumption and offer valuable insights for stakeholders aiming to optimize heating and cooling energy consumption in PCM-incorporated residential buildings.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Optimal Scheduling for Hydrogen-Enriched Integrated Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Hydrogen-enriched regional integrated energy systems (HRIES) have garnered significant attention in addressing climate-related issues. Incorporating Power-to-Hydrogen-Heat (P2HH) and Underground Hydrogen Storage (UHS) technologies into Hybrid Renewable Integrated Energy Systems (HRIES) is a viable solution for addressing seasonal fluctuations in energy supply. This study utilizes a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) methodology, which is based on empirical modeling, for effectively resolving the challenges in HRIES. The optimization procedure is defined through a Markov decision process, highlighting the dynamics between the agent and its surrounding environment. The research conclusively demonstrates the efficiency of the proposed scheduling technique and the increased adaptability of HRIES by integrating P2HH and UHS.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity and frequency Control Efficiency in AC islanded Microgrids: A Distributed Approach with a Stochastic Models
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper explores the vulnerability of AC islanded microgrids to cyber-attacks, focusing on communication links and local controls. Decentralized control methods are proposed to enhance security, with a detailed analysis of false data injection (FDI) and denial of service (DoS) attacks. Approaches to address DoS attacks include consensus of multiagent systems and risk-sensitive control. The study proposes a lightweight prevention model to mitigate FDI, featuring a cooperative stochastic control system with a communication-based controller. In contrast to existing distributed control methods, the proposed approach offers advantages in synchronizing frequency restoration, ensuring accurate power sharing through sparse communication networks, and reducing control update frequency. The study contributes to heightened system security, addresses limitations of centralized control methods, and integrates stationary proportional resonant primary control and intelligent secondary control based on the dragonfly algorithm for improved microgrid performance under various operating conditions.

articleTitle: An Adversarial-robust Graph Representation Learning for Energy-aware Vehicle Routing Considering Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The electrification of the transportation sector is increasingly recognized as a pivotal strategy for enhancing environmental sustainability, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and improving overall energy utilization. In this context, the development of vehicle routing solutions that are not only energy-efficient but also resilient to adversarial threats, and mindful of privacy considerations has become important. This paper introduces an innovative Graphormer-based model that adeptly balances energy efficiency, task sequencing, and privacy protection. Unlike traditional approaches that either neglect adversarial threats or employ simplistic energy scheduling, our model uniquely integrates Graph Neural Networks and Transformers to enhance global graphical information embedding to infer adversarial data. Under privacy protection, the regions instead of the exact locations of tasks are given. A mathematical model for the energy-aware vehicle routing problem that incorporates privacy protection is introduced, alongside a refined Graphormer model enhanced by three novel encoding structures: centrality encoding, spatial encoding, and edge encoding architectures. Through comprehensive simulations, our model not only achieves near-optimal solutions rapidly, adapting swiftly to environmental changes and adversarial attacks but also significantly surpasses existing benchmarks in energy efficiency and privacy preservation.

articleTitle: Identification of Sub/Super-synchronous Oscillation Parameters of Wind Power System Based on INMF Combined Blind Signal Separation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: With the development of power electronics technology, multi-machine coupling sub/super-synchronous oscillation accidents in wind power systems occur from time to time. Most of the common methods are aimed at the detection and identification of a single oscillation mode and are susceptible to noise interference. Mode aliasing will occur in oscillation identification when coupling is considered. In order to solve these problems, this paper proposes a sub/super-synchronous oscillation detection and parameter identification method based on improved non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) combined with blind signal separation, using synchronous squeeze transformation to improve the decomposition results of LOFAR spectra and enhance the aggregation degree within a short-time data window. Then, the blind signal separation algorithm is used to classify and sort the basis vectors obtained by decomposition, and the target signal is reconstructed. The parameters of the reconstructed signal are identified using the least squares rotation invariant technique (TLS-ESPRIT). Finally, the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper is verified through the composite signal testing and PSCAD/EMTDC electromagnetic simulation. The results show that the method proposed in this paper does not require additional noise reduction means, can more accurately extract coupled sub/super-synchronous oscillation(SSSO) signals, and has higher reliability in parameter identification results. Meanwhile, it provides help and reference for broadband oscillation detection and traceability of renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Quantifying the Influence and Projections of Zero-Carbon Smart Park Infrastructures on Urban Electricity Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In the pursuit of China's ambitious goals of achieving carbon neutrality and peak carbon emissions, the establishment of zero-carbon smart park stands out as a pivotal initiative. This study uses the panel regression model and the radial basis neural network model to study the relationship between these smart park and urban electricity consumption. We find that, for one thing, with the construction of zero-carbon smart park, urban electricity consumption increases 73.36, which exerts a significant and positive impact on urban electricity consumption; for another thing, the trained Radial Basis Neural Network model exhibits minimal error and robust predictive capabilities for forecasting urban electricity consumption. These results highlight the importance of constructing zero-carbon smart urban zones to manage and improve how cities consume energy, aligning with China's broader goals for sustainability.

Author Keywords: radial basis function neural network model

articleTitle: Research on the Interface Mechanism and Transaction Mode between “Energy use Rights and Carbon Emission Rights” and Green Electricity Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Driven by the goal of “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality”, China has remained committed to deepening the reform of institution, accelerated the construction of the market and improved the system of energy use rights, carbon emission rights (hereinafter referred to as the “two rights”) and the green power trading system continuously. As aforementioned, this paper introduces the “two rights” and green power trading model and designs the interface mechanism between green power trading and the “two rights”. Thereafter, a model for optimizing the new operating costs of typical enterprises participating in the green power trading market and the “two rights” market is proposed. Through the measurement and the cost analysis of a copper smelting enterprise in Jiangxi, China, it can be verified that enterprises can benefit from the participation in the “two rights” market and the green power trading market due to the interface mechanism. Thus, enterprises will participate in green power trading actively since the introduction of green power trading on the basis of the “two rights” market. Finally, this paper puts forward countermeasures and proposals for the interface mechanism between green power trading and the “two rights” market.

articleTitle: Investigation of Bifacial Gain and Albedo of Bifacial Photovoltaic Modules that Operate in a Tropical Site
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of ground materials and albedo on the performance of bifacial photovoltaic (PV) modules in tropical regions. This research holds significance as it fills a critical gap in the existing literature, providing a comprehensive exploration of bifacial gain and albedo in tropical regions using an experimental setup. The experimental setup involved the installation of monofacial and bifacial PV modules with standard installation practices commonly employed in Malaysia. Various ground materials-concrete, white gravel, soil, and grass-were placed beneath the panels to analyze their effects on module performance. At the end of the study, the results showed the potential of a bifacial PV system in the tropics. The calculated bifacial gain in this study ranges from 8.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> to 16.5%, depending on the ground materials applied. Compared to other bifacial PV system design research using only simulations, this paper emphasizes the importance of considering albedo variability, which could significantly impact bifacial gain in tropical regions. The results demonstrate a linear relationship between albedo and bifacial gain values. This study provides valuable insights for the PV industry, offering guidance in module selection for cost-effective PV plant installations. The calculated albedo and bifacial gain will serve as the reference range for the PV industry.

articleTitle: Assessing the Viability of Renewable Energy Integration in Battery Swappable Conversion Kits for Tuk-tuks in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Tuk-tuks are a widely favored means of transportation for both passengers and cargo in Sri Lanka. Their affordability in terms of purchase price and maintenance, coupled with good mileage, has contributed to their popularity. However, this popularity comes with significant drawbacks, notably high emissions and a surge in the number of vehicles on the roads. Therefore, the transportation sector has started to look towards electric alternatives. However, the increasing adoption of electric vehicles pose a potential challenge to the Sri Lankan power generation sector, which heavily relies on fossil fuel-based thermal power generation. To address these issues, this feasibility study seeks to evaluate the feasibility of implementing a conversion kit that enables existing tuk-tuks to operate on electricity, incorporating battery-swapping technology and charging stations powered by solar photovoltaic systems. The study extensively examines the performance characteristics of currently available commercial electric tuk-tuks and provides a detailed comparison of each model available in the local market. In the electrification of the tuk-tuks, the range anxiety is another major drawback. Therefore, in this study we have compared the existing electric tuk-tuk solutions and proposed and evaluated the most feasible solution for electrification of tuk-tuks in Sri Lanka which is the battery swappable conversion kit.

articleTitle: Resilience Enhancement of Renewable Energy High Penetration Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The increasing permeability of renewable energy stands out as a prominent trend in the evolution of modern power systems. Nevertheless, the frequent occurrence of severe climate conditions and the vulnerability of renewable power constitute a significant obstacle to the resilience of electricity systems. Acting as a pivotal technology supporting renewables, energy storage systems play a crucial role in fortifying the resilience of power systems. Existing research on energy storage systems that enhance resilience is mostly ground-based and only addresses short-term need. This study introduces a method to enhance recovery capacity of electric networks featuring a sizable permeability of renewable power, focusing on underground energy storage systems (UESS). To begin with, formulate an assessment model for resilience, wherein the impact of severe climate conditions is measured by the breakdown frequencies of electric grid modules. Subsequently, a two-layer optimal model is developed to govern the operation and planning of UESS in the face of extreme weather conditions, taking into account the life cycle of the underground energy storage systems. Finally, utilizing a 9-node power system with a high permeability of renewable energy as a case study, present the optimal configuration and operation scheme for UESS and analyze the investment and benefits. The findings highlight that UESS can notably bolster the resilience of power systems during extreme weather events.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm-Based Path Planning for Refrigeration Plant Room Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The refrigeration room has numerous pipelines, and the spatial layout is rather intricate. Most of the existing refrigeration room pipeline designs are manually created, resulting in low efficiency. This study is based on the fundamental principles of reducing system resistance, optimizing space utilization, and avoiding pipeline collisions. It employs a genetic algorithm for the automatic arrangement of pipeline spatial pathways. This algorithm models the refrigeration room, encodes each coordinate point, and evaluates the quality of pathways based on criteria such as pipeline length, the number of bends, obstacle avoidance, and pipeline compactness. Through case studies, the results demonstrate the feasibility of this approach in refrigeration room pipeline design. This algorithm can address the challenge of determining the optimal pipeline spatial pathway in complex scenarios, where manual decision-making is difficult. Combining artificial intelligence algorithms with design practices can revolutionize traditional design methods and enhance design efficiency.
